key_insight: An exciton-kinetics coupled drift-diffusion model shows that CT-CS energy alignment is the dominant lever controlling the trade-off between charge generation and voltage loss in organic photovoltaics.
engineering_relevance: The model gives device designers actionable energy-offset targets for optimizing both photocurrent extraction and open-circuit voltage in singlet/triplet-mediated OPV blends.
method: Self-consistently couples exciton state kinetics with drift-diffusion charge transport.
Solves singlet and triplet populations with reversible photophysical transitions for transient and steady-state response.
Tests how LE-CT, CT-CS, and LE-T offsets plus triplet-transfer rates affect generation, recombination, and voltage loss.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful reproduction of triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends, with design rules derived from the simulations.
watch_item: Predicted performance is highly sensitive to CT-CS alignment and triplet-recycling kinetics, so inaccurate energetic parameters or temperature dependence could shift the optimal design window.
paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
